A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GeoWorld and contain complete corresponding main sections, references, and 13-page supplementary material. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support a reliable comparison of all 25 pages.

before.justification: v1 reports original GeoWorld experiments on CrossTask and COIN in main Tables 1–3, plus component ablations, geometric analyses, and extended-horizon results in the supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and supplementary analyses, with revised numerical results in main Tables 1 and 2.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 retain the same Hyperbolic JEPA, teacher-forcing and rollout losses, geometric reinforcement learning, triangle-inequality regularization, and CEM planning procedure.

E1.justification: Training sources and CrossTask/COIN image- and video-conditioned planning coverage are unchanged. Both versions include the supplementary CrossTask evaluations extending to T=8.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within each main and supplementary experiment, including all four V-JEPA 2 scales. Revised baseline scores do not introduce or remove comparison methods.

E3.justification: The reported metrics, planning horizons, model scales, training schedules, encoder controls, and CEM settings are unchanged. No protocol alteration is documented for the revised scores.

E4.justification: The energy-landscape and hyperbolicity analyses, encoder fine-tuning comparisons, SFT/GRL ablations, hyperparameter sweeps, and extended-horizon tests are identical, including supplementary Sections 4–6.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged. Revised benchmark entries remain point estimates, without added run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Main Table 1 raises V-JEPA 2 COIN mIoUs by 20–25 points, substantially narrowing GeoWorld's advantages. For ViT-g384 at T=3, V-JEPA 2 changes from 64.53 to 89.53 while GeoWorld remains 89.88, shrinking the gap from 25.35 to 0.35 points. Main Table 2 lowers COIN T=4 mIoUs for all V-JEPA 2 and GeoWorld scales by 1–4 points; their ViT-g384 values change from 94.51 to 90.51 and 95.84 to 91.84, respectively. Reported settings, SR, mAcc, CrossTask results, and supplementary results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations, and derivations are identical, including hyperbolic maps and distances, the path-value formulation, and triangle-inequality regularization. No proofs or assumptions are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same H-JEPA/GRL contributions and claims of approximately 3% SR improvement at T=3 and 2% at T=4. The mIoU revisions do not alter these stated claims.

C2.justification: The results discussion and supplementary Sections 6–7 retain the same geometric-drift explanation and qualifications about implicit future-branching hierarchies and future embodied applications. No interpretation of the revised mIoUs is added.

D1.justification: Architecture details, optimization settings, curvature parameterization, hardware, CEM hyperparameters, and the project link are unchanged. No new implementation or reproducibility information accompanies the score revisions.

R1.justification: The same 88 references and research positioning are retained, including the related-work discussion and supplementary baseline descriptions.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp changes from v1, 26 February 2026, to v2, 17 May 2026. Body prose, headings, terminology, and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, table structures, captions, highlighting, and placement are unchanged. Tables 1 and 2 replace numerical values within identical layouts; all supplementary pages render identically.

improvement.justification: The revised COIN mIoUs materially alter comparative margins, but v2 provides no explanation or corroborating evidence establishing whether these replacements correct earlier errors. Methods, success-rate results, claims, uncertainty reporting, and supplementary evidence remain unchanged. The PDFs therefore do not establish whether the numerical revisions improve reporting reliability or overall paper quality.
